providers.description: RapidSOS operates what it calls "the world's largest Safety Network," an intelligent safety platform that connects public safety agencies (911 / ECCs), enterprises, and hundreds of millions of connected devices to deliver AI-powered emergency detection, verification, and escalation for faster, more informed emergency response. RapidSOS exposes partner APIs so technology partners can send emergency-related information into the safety platform and public-safety partners can consume incident data, alongside products including Alerts and IAR (IamResponding). The developer documentation at developer.rapidsos.com is partner-login gated and RapidSOS does not publish an open OpenAPI specification. Backed by Insight Partners and Playground Global.

providers.name: Local Logic
providers.description: Local Logic is a location intelligence platform for real estate, founded in 2015, that turns 100B+ data points across 250 million addresses in the US and Canada into 18 proprietary location scores, points of interest, demographics, school ratings, market statistics, value drivers, and climate-risk signals. Its REST API at api.locallogic.co exposes Location Scores, Profiles, Geographies, Points of Interest, Demographics, Schools, Value Drivers, Similar Neighborhoods, Location Snapshot, Market Statistics, and Climate Risk endpoints to real estate brokerages, portals, lenders, and proptech platforms, authenticated with a client ID and secret.

providers.name: University of Minnesota
providers.description: The University of Minnesota is a public land-grant research university with its flagship campus in the Twin Cities (Minneapolis-Saint Paul), ranked #203 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its developer/API footprint is led by the OIT Integrations Team, which publishes a suite of "Common Good APIs" sourced from the University's Common Data Layer (CDL) covering person, HR, student, class, and organization data; access requires request and data-custodian approval. Additional public-facing APIs include the University Libraries digital collection APIs (UMedia JSON and IIIF) and GEMS Informatics agricultural/geospatial data APIs. Most data APIs are gated behind access requests and institutional authentication.

providers.name: Bureau of Indian Affairs
providers.description: The Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) is the oldest bureau in the U.S. Department of the Interior. Its mission is to enhance the quality of life, promote economic opportunity, and carry out the federal responsibility to protect and improve the trust assets of American Indians, Indian tribes, and Alaska Natives. The BIA administers services directly or through contracts, grants, and compacts with 574 federally recognized tribes serving approximately 2.5 million people. BIA publishes geospatial datasets, directories, and forms through the Indian Affairs GIS Open Data portal, the Tribal Leader Directory, and official agency websites.

providers.name: BetterView Marketplace
providers.description: Betterview is a market-leading Property Intelligence platform that delivers actionable insights to property & casualty insurance underwriters, agents, and insureds to increase efficiency and profitability. Its API lets carriers order and retrieve property profiles enriched with the Roof Spotlight Index (RSI), peril risks, flags, and third-party Partner Connect data, subscribe properties to PropertyPulse monitoring, and query PropertyNow pre-processed datasets by address or coordinates. Betterview integrates with core insurance systems including Guidewire (a Marketplace accelerator for PolicyCenter 10), Duck Creek, and Socotra, and supports SSO, Secure FTP, ImageRight drop, an embeddable geospatial iframe UI, and an External Data Warehouse (EDW) SQL connection.

providers.name: BreezoMeter
providers.description: Environmental intelligence REST API providing real-time and forecast air quality, pollen counts, wildfire data, and weather information with street-level accuracy. BreezoMeter was acquired by Google in September 2022 and its technology is now integrated into Google Maps Platform.

providers.name: OurAirports
providers.description: OurAirports is an open airport data platform maintained by a global community of aviation enthusiasts. It provides a comprehensive, community-maintained database of 85,000+ airports, runways, radio navigation aids (navaids), and communication frequencies worldwide. All data is released to the public domain and is available as daily-updated CSV datasets hosted on GitHub Pages. The platform covers airports of every type — from large commercial hubs to small private airstrips, heliports, seaplane bases, and balloon ports — across every country and territory on Earth.

providers.name: Wyvern
providers.description: Wyvern is a Canadian space technology company operating the world's first commercial hyperspectral satellite constellation. Its Dragonette satellites deliver 31-band VNIR imagery at 5.3 metre ground sampling distance for agriculture, forestry, energy, mining, and defence use cases. Wyvern publishes an Open Data Program of free hyperspectral imagery delivered as a public STAC 1.0.0 catalog, alongside a knowledge centre, data product guide, and open notebooks for working with its imagery.

providers.name: Texas A&M University
providers.description: Texas A&M University is a public land-grant research university in College Station, Texas, and the flagship of the Texas A&M University System. It is ranked #154 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public developer footprint is led by the Texas A&M University System API Developer Portal (api-doc.sea.system.tamus.edu), which exposes gated enterprise services such as the UIN Services API behind subscription approval, alongside the publicly documented TAMU GeoServices geocoding/address API and an active library open-source ecosystem on GitHub (TAMULib) covering IIIF, DSpace, and Vireo ETD systems.

providers.name: Wikimapia
providers.description: Wikimapia is a collaborative geographic wiki that layers crowdsourced place information onto satellite imagery. Launched in 2006, the platform covers over 32 million geographic objects contributed by its community. The REST API provides programmatic access to places, categories, streets, and geographic searches using API-key authentication. Responses are available in JSON and KML formats. The API supports bounding-box queries, coordinate-based nearest-place lookups, full-text search, and detailed place retrieval including geometry, photos, comments, and community-tagged categories.

providers.name: Baidu
providers.description: Baidu is a leading Chinese internet and artificial-intelligence company whose developer surface spans three main product lines. Baidu AI Cloud "Qianfan" is a Model-as-a-Service platform hosting the ERNIE model family behind an OpenAI-compatible REST API for chat, embeddings, and agent building (AppBuilder). The Baidu AI Open Platform exposes OCR, NLP, speech, face, image, and knowledge-graph APIs. The Baidu Maps Open Platform (LBS) provides geocoding, place search, route planning, weather, and real-time traffic to millions of registered developers, and ships an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with a hosted remote endpoint. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company and enriched with real, first-party developer artifacts.

providers.name: Irth Solutions
providers.description: Irth Solutions is a SaaS platform provider for critical-infrastructure damage prevention, asset (pipeline) integrity, and stakeholder land management, trusted by energy, utility, and telecom operators across the U.S. and Canada since 1995. Its products include 811 ticket management (UtiliSphere, Exactix, and 811spotter for contractors), one-call center notification, intelligent forms and workflows, inline-inspection and corrosion/crack asset-integrity analytics, and lease, royalty, and right-of-way land management, powered by business intelligence, analytics, and geospatial data. Irth exposes a RESTful Integration API (Irthnet / UtiliSphere) secured with a per-integration API key for creating and modifying users, map layers, and work items in real time.

providers.name: CeresAI
providers.description: CeresAI (formerly Ceres Imaging) is an aerial and satellite agricultural intelligence platform that converts high-resolution spectral imagery and machine learning into field-level insights on crop health, water stress, yield, and financial risk. The company serves growers, agribusinesses, lenders, and crop-insurance providers across more than 40 crop types on four continents, drawing on billions of plant-level data points to support yield protection, sustainability scorecards, portfolio risk analysis, and insurance claims. CeresAI operates a customer application and a login-gated developer documentation portal at dev.ceres.ai; pricing is consultation-based rather than self-serve. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: FloodMapp
providers.description: FloodMapp is a flood intelligence technology company that provides real-time, impact-based flood forecasting and mapping for emergency managers, government agencies, and critical infrastructure operators. Its AI-driven hydrology and hydraulics models deliver street-level (1-meter resolution) flood impact forecasts, updated hourly, 24/7/365, using live rainfall, river and coastal gauge networks, and terrain data. Capabilities ship as three products — ForeCast (predictive), NowCast (real-time), and PostCast (post-event) — packaged into PREPARE and RESPOND solutions. FloodMapp delivers its data as GIS-native live feeds (OGC WMS/WFS layers) that integrate directly into Esri ArcGIS, ArcGIS Online, Google, Mapbox, and QGIS. The authenticated API surface at api.floodmapp.com is protected by AWS Cognito OAuth2/OIDC. FloodMapp is SOC 2 Type II certified and serves customers across the United States and Australia.

providers.name: dClimate
providers.description: dClimate is a chain-agnostic, decentralized climate information ecosystem that makes it easy for businesses, governments, and builders to find, access, and utilize essential data about the planet. Rather than a conventional REST API, dClimate exposes its weather and climate data SDK-first over content-addressed (IPFS/IPLD) storage: official Python and JavaScript clients resolve datasets from a STAC catalog and stream sharded Zarr stores, requiring no API key or OAuth for public data. Offerings span weather/climate reanalysis and forecast sources such as ECMWF ERA5 and AIFS, a Data Marketplace featuring datasets from providers like NASA and ESA, plus the Aegis and CYCLOPS climate-intelligence platforms. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Overpass API
providers.description: Overpass API is a read-only OpenStreetMap data API that enables querying geographic features including nodes, ways, relations, and tags using the Overpass Query Language (QL). It supports complex spatial queries with filters for bounding boxes, tags, proximity, area containment, and element relationships, making it the primary tool for extracting custom subsets of OSM data programmatically.

providers.name: Attentive.ai
providers.description: Attentive.ai builds AI-powered software for the construction and outdoor services industries, automating property measurements, takeoffs, and estimating from aerial imagery and blueprints. Its Automeasure platform measures properties from satellite and site-plan imagery for landscaping, paving, and snow-removal contractors, while Beam AI (ibeam.ai) automates construction takeoffs and estimates and BIM CoPilot handles modeling, clash detection, and as-built documentation. The company is backed by Insight Partners. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; Attentive.ai does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition, so this record captures its identity, security posture, and site link properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Naver
providers.description: Naver Corp. is South Korea's largest internet company, operating the Naver search portal, Naver Webtoon, Naver Pay, Naver Maps, Naver Shopping, WORKS Mobile, and the LINE messenger platform (jointly with SoftBank via LY Corporation). Naver runs two distinct public developer surfaces: Naver Developers (developers.naver.com) which hosts Naver's classic Open APIs — Search (blog, news, book, encyclopedia, café, knowledge, web, image, shop, doc), Papago N2MT translation, Naver Login (OAuth 2.0), Naver Maps geocoding and static map, Datalab trend, CAPTCHA, and SmartEditor; and Naver Cloud Platform (www.ncloud.com) — Naver's IaaS / PaaS offering with Compute (Server, Container, Functions), Storage (Object, Block, File), Network (VPC, CDN+, Global Edge), AI (CLOVA Speech, CLOVA OCR, Papago, HyperCLOVA X), Maps, SENS (SMS / push messaging), Cloud Search, and Certificate Manager.

providers.name: ENMAX
providers.description: ENMAX Corporation is the Calgary-based energy company owned outright by The City of Calgary, describing itself on its own about page as "a regulated wires company, a competitive power generator and an energy retailer" operating "across Alberta and Maine." It spans three tiers of the value chain at once: ENMAX Power owns and operates the regulated electricity distribution and transmission system inside Calgary, ENMAX Energy generates power and sells electricity and natural gas into Alberta's deregulated retail market under the Easymax brand, and Versant Power — acquired from Emera in 2020 — is the transmission and distribution utility for northern and eastern Maine. Its API posture is the exact inverse of the Ontario utilities it is usually compared to, and the inversion is the finding. No consumer energy data mandate binds ENMAX anywhere it operates: Alberta has no Green Button regulation, Ontario's O. Reg. 633/21 does not reach across the provincial border, Canada has no national equivalent, and Maine imposes no Green Button obligation on Versant Power. Unmandated, ENMAX built nothing — its own support documentation states plainly that the Energy Insights usage view inside a customer's Easymax account "is view-only within your online account and can't be exported at this time," which is a harder closure than most: not merely no API, but no CSV, no XML, and no Green Button either. There is no developer portal, no developer, api, docs or data subdomain, no OpenAPI, and no published third-party data path. What ENMAX does publish openly is grid data. Its Hosting Capacity, Load Capacity and Service Area maps, linked from enmax.com/system-resources, are ArcGIS Online web applications backed by ArcGIS REST feature services that answer anonymous machine-readable queries with no key, no signup and no terms — distribution-feeder DER hosting headroom and remaining load capacity for the Calgary service territory, the data a solar or storage developer actually needs. ENMAX never calls this an API and documents none of it, but it is real, it is open, and it is queryable. Wide open on grid data, completely shut on customer data.

providers.name: Parkopedia
providers.description: With the roll-out of connected cars, services such as live traffic and live parking have become standard requirements. Parkopedia leads the market in parking data services, with 90 million parking spaces globally across 90 countries, available via the Parkopedia parking API or feed.

providers.name: Life360
providers.description: Life360 is a family safety platform built around a location-sharing mobile app for iOS and Android, offering real-time member location, Place Alerts, location history, driving safety scores and trip history, crash detection, SOS alerts and emergency dispatch, plus digital safety features such as identity theft protection and dark web monitoring. Its hardware line, following the acquisitions of Tile and Jiobit, spans Tile Mate, Pro, Slim and Sticker Bluetooth item trackers and a cellular GPS pet tracker, sold direct and through Amazon, Best Buy, Target and Walmart. The service is sold as Free, Silver, Gold and Platinum membership tiers. Life360 publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI, no SDKs and no developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is an agent-facing one (llms.txt, an ai-plugin manifest whose advertised OpenAPI does not resolve, and Content-Signal directives in robots.txt). This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Overture Maps Foundation
providers.description: The Overture Maps Foundation is a Linux Foundation project created in partnership with Meta, Microsoft, AWS, and TomTom to build reliable, open map data as an alternative to proprietary mapping platforms. It provides openly available datasets for places, buildings, transportation, and administrative boundaries.

providers.name: Overture Maps Foundation
providers.description: Overture Maps Foundation is a Linux Foundation collaborative project that produces free, open, and interoperable map data. Overture publishes cloud-native GeoParquet datasets, on a regular release cadence, across six themes - Addresses, Base, Buildings, Divisions, Places, and Transportation - governed by a common conflation pipeline and an open schema. Rather than a hosted REST API, Overture distributes data through Amazon S3 and Microsoft Azure (and via partner mirrors on BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, Fused, Wherobots), and provides an open Python CLI, a tile generator, and an Explorer site for developers. Founding members include Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and TomTom.

providers.name: NDBC — National Data Buoy Center
providers.description: The NOAA National Data Buoy Center (NDBC) operates a global network of over 1,000 moored buoys, drifting buoys, Coastal-Marine Automated Network (C-MAN) stations, and partner stations that continuously measure and transmit meteorological and oceanographic conditions. Real-time and historical data — wind direction and speed, wave height and period, sea surface temperature, atmospheric pressure, air temperature, dew point, visibility, and salinity — are distributed freely via HTTP file URLs, a THREDDS/OPeNDAP server (NetCDF), an RSS observation feed, and a latest-observations snapshot updated every five minutes. No API key or authentication is required; data is in the public domain under U.S. government open-data policy.

providers.name: REalyse
providers.description: REalyse is a UK residential property data platform that aggregates more than 100 data sources into geospatial analysis and market-intelligence tools for developers, lenders, investors, consultants, and funds. Its data spans five domains — Planning & Policy, Demographics, Market (rental and sales pricing, yields, days on market, comparables), Land & Ownership, and Amenities. REalyse offers a data API for institutions that require a constant feed of property data, alongside the REalyse Core geospatial platform, the REalyse Pulse consumer AI valuation product, and downloadable Market Intelligence reports. The company is based in London and is backed by Anthemis. API access is onboarded through the sales team rather than a self-service developer portal, so no public OpenAPI, base URL, or authentication reference is published.

providers.name: Urban SDK
providers.description: Urban SDK is a geospatial AI and data analytics company serving the public sector, delivering hourly road-speed and traffic data, analytics, and AI tools that help cities, counties, and transportation agencies prioritize issues, pinpoint trends, and act on traffic management, public safety, emergency response, and infrastructure planning. A Techstars portfolio company based in Jacksonville, Florida, Urban SDK delivers its data through a web platform and automated Workflows reports rather than a public API, and currently publishes no developer documentation or client SDKs.

providers.name: UrbanFootprint
providers.description: UrbanFootprint is a resilient decision intelligence platform that delivers urban, climate, and community-resilience data and analytics, helping governments, utilities, financial institutions, and planners assess risk and make data-driven decisions. Its platform spans scenario analysis (Analyst), map-based data exploration (Explorer), and curated data subscriptions covering climate hazards, the built environment, and social vulnerability. UrbanFootprint is a closed SaaS platform sold via sales contact and publishes no public developer API; its application authenticates through Auth0 and consumes an internal platform API.

providers.name: WindBorne Systems
providers.description: WindBorne Systems operates a global constellation of long-duration Global Sounding Balloons and pairs that proprietary in-situ atmospheric data with WeatherMesh, its AI-based numerical weather forecast model. The WindBorne Data API serves real-time balloon observations, soundings, super-observations, constellation and flight-path metadata, point and gridded WeatherMesh forecasts, tropical-cyclone tracks, and population-weighted heating/cooling degree-day insights. Access is via a Bearer API key over REST, an official Python library and CLI, and a hosted Model Context Protocol server for AI agents.

providers.name: Cape Analytics
providers.description: Cape Analytics (now part of Moody's) is a geospatial property intelligence provider that applies computer vision and machine learning to high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, property records, and other novel data sources to produce inspection-quality condition and characteristic data for over 100 million residential and commercial structures across the United States and Canada. Its insights — roof condition and material, swimming pools, solar panels, accessory structures, tree overhang, wildfire and wind exposure, distance to hazards, and a proprietary Liquidity Score — are delivered to insurance underwriters, lenders, and real estate investors in under two seconds via API, batch/bulk files, an Automated Property Condition Report (aPCR), and a customer web portal, as well as through third-party platforms such as Guidewire and Duck Creek. Cape does not publish a public, self-service developer portal or open API specification; API access is provisioned to customers and partners through a gated onboarding flow.

providers.name: Spire Global
providers.description: Spire Global operates a constellation of more than 100 LEMUR nanosatellites collecting maritime AIS, aviation ADS-B, GNSS-RO weather profiles, and RF geolocation data, and offers Space Services for hosted payloads and managed satellite missions. Its data products are exposed as developer-friendly APIs: Spire Maritime 2.0 (now operated by Kpler) delivers vessel-tracking AIS through a GraphQL endpoint; Spire Aviation publishes REST APIs and real-time streams for flight metadata, live ADS-B tracking, historic positions, and event feeds; Spire Weather and Climate provides RESTful weather and ocean data APIs including 30 years of maritime weather history; and Spire Space Services exposes a developer portal for managed satellite operations. Spire's APIs are documented at product-specific subdomains and authenticated with API keys.

providers.name: Beeline
providers.description: Beeline makes smart navigation devices and a companion mobile app for cyclists and motorcyclists. Its compact handlebar-mounted devices — Beeline Velo for bicycles and Beeline Moto for motorcycles — use a simple directional and turn-by-turn interface to help riders find their way around towns and cities, discover better routes, and record their journeys. The London-based company is backed by Seedcamp. Beeline sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted storefront at beeline.co, which exposes an agent-facing commerce surface — a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint, Shopify customer-account OIDC, and an llms.txt agent policy — rather than a first-party developer product API.

providers.name: Molekule
providers.description: Molekule is a consumer air-quality hardware company that makes FDA-cleared HEPA air purifiers for homes and businesses. It sells direct-to-consumer through molekule.com, a Shopify-hosted storefront. While Molekule does not publish a traditional developer API, its store exposes a live agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp for AI shopping agents, OpenID Connect buyer authentication via the Shopify Customer Account API, and published agent instructions at /agents.md and /llms.txt. This profile captures that machine-readable commerce surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SafeGraph
providers.description: SafeGraph is a geospatial data company that builds and maintains high-quality Point of Interest (POI), building geometry, and geocoded address datasets used for location intelligence, site selection, competitive analysis, and machine-learning models. Its core products are Places (millions of POIs with base, rich, and premium attributes), Geometry (building-footprint polygons), Address (structured geocoded addresses across 25+ countries), and Spend (transaction data). Rather than a hosted REST API, SafeGraph delivers data as bulk parquet files via S3, Snowflake, AWS Data Exchange, CARTO, Databricks, and ArcGIS. Surfaced originally as a Sapphire Ventures portfolio company and enriched here from SafeGraph's public documentation, changelog, and packages.

providers.name: RoxyAPI
providers.description: Multi-domain spiritual intelligence API exposing 164+ endpoints across 12 domains (Western Astrology, Vedic Astrology, Numerology, Tarot, Human Design, Forecast, Biorhythm, I-Ching, Crystals, Dreams, Angel Numbers, Location/Timezone) under a single API key. Powered by the proprietary Roxy Ephemeris engine verified against NASA JPL Horizons DE441. Offers REST API, OpenAPI 3.1 contract, per-domain remote MCP servers, llms.txt, and an AGENTS.md agent playbook.

providers.name: Bikemap
providers.description: Bikemap is a Vienna-based cycling platform (backed by Speedinvest) offering a route planner, turn-by-turn bike navigation, and one of the world's largest communities of user-generated cycling routes across road, mountain, gravel, and e-bike riding. Riders plan routes in a web and mobile route editor, discover millions of community routes, record and share rides, download offline maps, and sync with Garmin, Wahoo, Apple Watch, and Wear OS devices. Bikemap operates a consumer product surface (web, iOS, Android) and does not publish a documented public developer API; this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Descartes Labs
providers.description: Descartes Labs was a Santa Fe, New Mexico geospatial intelligence company founded in 2014 as a spin-out from Los Alamos National Laboratory. The company built the Descartes Labs Platform, a cloud-native geospatial data refinery and analytics environment combining a petabyte-scale satellite imagery archive (Landsat, Sentinel-1/2, MODIS, NAIP, PlanetScope, SkySat, commercial radar, NEXRAD weather radar, plus client-uploaded data) with a Python client library, JupyterHub-based workbench, and distributed compute for training and running deep learning and remote-sensing models at scale. Customers in agriculture, mining, energy, defense, insurance, and the U.S. government used the platform to build production geospatial machine learning pipelines covering crop forecasting, mineral exploration, infrastructure monitoring, methane detection, wildfire response, and ESG reporting. The Platform exposed a Catalog (imagery, bands, products, blobs, events), a Compute service (containerised functions, jobs, schedules), a Vector service (tabular and geospatial features), Dynamic Compute (lazy raster algebra and tiling), Auth, and a `descarteslabs` CLI. In October 2024, EarthDaily Analytics — backed by Antarctica Capital — acquired Descartes Labs and the Descartes Labs Government, Inc. subsidiary, folding the team, customers, and platform into the EarthDaily Constellation programme. The product was rebranded EarthOne in 2025; the `descarteslabs` Python package has been formally discontinued in favour of `earthdaily-earthone` (v5.x), the github.com/descarteslabs organisation has been renamed to `dlarchives`, www.descarteslabs.com is now a parked domain, and the docs.descarteslabs.com developer portal has been retired in favour of EarthDaily-hosted EarthOne documentation. This catalog entry preserves the historical Descartes Labs Platform surface as an archive — see the EarthDaily / EarthOne profile for the active product.

providers.name: NATIX
providers.description: NATIX Network is a decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN) network building what it calls the world's largest on-street camera network to power Physical AI, autonomous driving, and real-time mapping. Drivers use the Drive& smartphone app and the VX360 plug-and-earn smart camera for Tesla to collect, validate, anonymize, and monetize multi-camera dashcam footage, earning $NATIX token rewards. NATIX packages the resulting data into training datasets, edge cases, and OpenScenario/OpenDrive simulation scenarios for AI and mapping customers, and runs an on-chain token economy with staking, governance, and xNodes. As of 2026 it reports 2.89M+ registered drivers and coverage across 33 countries. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment confirms NATIX publishes no public REST/GraphQL developer API — the surface is consumer apps, an on-chain token, and a proprietary partner Vision SDK.

providers.name: Premise
providers.description: Premise is a global data-intelligence platform that combines machine learning with a distributed network of on-the-ground human contributors to collect, structure, and analyze local ground-truth data across 140+ countries. The platform reports 6M+ contributors, 25M+ submissions per year, and 2.3M+ unique points of interest, and serves three primary markets: precision mapping and geospatial intelligence, international development, and public-sector organizations. Premise is a portfolio company of a16z, Anthemis, and GV. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; data is delivered through managed engagements and its customer platform.

providers.name: PSD Citywide
providers.description: PSD Citywide is a SaaS provider of enterprise asset management (EAM) and public-sector software for North American municipalities and government organizations. Its integrated Citywide platform spans asset management, maintenance and work-order management, GIS integration (ESRI-powered mapping), permitting, planning and licensing with citizen portals, multi-year budgeting and forecasting, facility/space management (Spaces), and a field mobile app, alongside asset-management advisory and grant services. The homepage references a "robust API" for integration and customization, but no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization were found during enrichment; end-user product documentation is published in a HappyFox-powered help center. Added to the API Evangelist network via the norwest-venture-partners portfolio.

providers.name: Aino World Inc.
providers.description: Aino World Inc. builds Aino, an AI-powered spatial analytics platform for architecture, urban planning, and real estate development teams. Aino automates site research by pulling zoning, parcel, transit, demographic, and environmental data from 10+ sources (Google Maps, Regrid, Rentcast, OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps, Microsoft Planetary Computer, Kontur.io, and the US Census), runs GIS-free spatial analysis, and generates presentation-ready maps and dashboards inside a shared, collaborative workspace. Coverage spans 400+ cities with thousands of reusable data layers and CAD/GeoJSON (DXF) exports. Backed by 500 Global. Programmatic API access is offered on the enterprise Business tier.

providers.name: OnStation
providers.description: OnStation is a digital stationing platform for road and highway construction projects, replacing paper station logs and manual chaining with GPS-based field documentation. Its iOS and Android mobile app lets crews, inspectors, and project managers identify exact station locations, drop and share flags, capture timestamped photos and notes, and complete forms in the field without extra hardware. A cloud Data Portal aggregates that field documentation into searchable, exportable DOT-ready reports for compliance and dispute resolution, while Active Worksite alerts drivers through Waze and OEM systems when crews are working. OnStation offers pre-built integrations with construction and survey systems including HCSS HeavyJob, Trimble and Bad Elf GNSS receivers, TransTech density gauges, FleetWatcher e-ticketing, and ESRI GIS, but does not currently publish a public developer API. Backed by Insight Partners and Techstars.

providers.name: Kayrros
providers.description: Kayrros is an environmental-intelligence and geospatial-AI company that independently tracks human activity and its physical footprint worldwide by combining satellite imagery, alternative data, and machine learning. Its products span energy markets — crude oil and jet fuel intelligence, LNG, renewables, solar and battery-storage construction monitoring, industrial and on-road energy demand, and stockpiles — and environmental risk — methane emissions via Methane Watch, wildfire risk, forest-carbon and deforestation monitoring, and carbon accounting. Kayrros delivers asset-level data feeds, APIs, and dashboards to traders, operators, financial institutions, regulators, insurers, and the public sector. The company was acquired by Energy Aspects in May 2026.

providers.name: Agreena
providers.description: Agreena is a Copenhagen-based agtech and climate finance company, founded in 2021, that helps farmers transition to regenerative agriculture and monetize the resulting soil-carbon outcomes. Its AgreenaCarbon platform combines farmer enrollment, a satellite-, AI-, and soil-sampling-based digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV) engine, and Verra-certified carbon credit issuance. Agreena also offers standalone remote-sensing products such as a field-boundary-detection API for agrifood supply-chain monitoring. The platform spans roughly 5 million hectares and 2,500+ farmers across ~20 European countries. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and HV Capital and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agreena publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI surface at this time.

providers.name: Sunairio
providers.description: Sunairio is a grid forecasting company that provides integrated weather, climate, and energy insights for power markets. Its flagship platform, Sunairio ONE, generates 1,000-member ensemble forecasts across horizons from hourly to decadal, capturing extreme-weather and grid-stress scenarios that traditional forecasts miss. The company also publishes SHED (Sunairio High-resolution Earth Data), a proprietary historical weather dataset for the Continental US from 1950 to present at roughly 100x the resolution of ERA5, with asset-level wind and solar variability. Customers such as energy traders, grid operators, utility-scale asset developers, and demand-response aggregators access forecasts and data through a web UI, an API, and (on higher tiers) direct Snowflake data delivery. Founded in 2020 by Rob Cirincione, the company has been recognized by the National Science Foundation, American Clean Power, and EPRI.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: Vodafone
providers.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

providers.name: Upciti
providers.description: Upciti is a French smart-city company that equips cities with intelligent computer-vision sensors and the Upciti OS platform, turning streets into clear, anonymous data for informed municipal decisions across parking, mobility, energy, water, gas, lighting, temperature, weather, air quality, pollen, illegal dumping, and noise. Sensors process video 100% locally with no image storage (GDPR-native, DTPR-supporting), and the platform advertises an open API for connecting GIS, BI, and business tools with no proprietary lock-in. Product documentation is customer-gated.

providers.name: GEODNET
providers.description: GEODNET (Global Earth Observation Decentralized Network) is a Web3/DePIN blockchain-based RTK (Real-Time Kinematics) GNSS correction network. It incentivizes operators to deploy permanent GNSS reference stations ("Satellite Miners") that broadcast real-time correction data, letting nearby devices achieve centimeter-level positioning accuracy. Station operators earn GEOD token rewards, with a target of 100,000 evenly distributed base stations worldwide — roughly twenty times larger than existing CORS networks. The correction data fuels robots, drones, autonomous vehicles, precision agriculture, construction, surveying, and consumer mapping. Developer-facing surfaces are the GEODNET Console web platform, the RTK coverage service, and DAO governance; the GEOD token spans Polygon and Solana. This profile was seeded as a Multicoin Capital portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Aclima
providers.description: Aclima is a San Francisco-based environmental intelligence company that maps and analyzes air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions at hyperlocal, block-by-block resolution. Using a network of roving (vehicle-mounted) and stationary sensors, Aclima measures multiple pollutants and climate gases simultaneously at up to 100,000x greater resolution than traditional monitoring, then translates billions of scientific measurements into environmental intelligence for governments, companies, and communities. Its professional analytics software, Aclima Pro, delivers visualization and automated analytics for emissions reduction and public-health programs, while its free air.health app maps address-level air and climate insights for the communities Aclima serves. Co-founded by CEO Davida Herzl, Aclima is backed by DCVC and is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Neara
providers.description: Neara is a physics-enabled digital twin platform for electric utilities and network operators. It builds a single, physics-accurate 3D model of a utility's entire network from LiDAR, GIS, and imagery, then runs engineering-grade simulations across vegetation management, wildfire and flood mitigation, severe-weather response, clearance and conductor-clash analysis, pole utilization and FEA, asset inspection and lifecycle management, and transmission and distribution network design. Utilities use Neara to plan, harden, and operate their grids at scale — forecasting and backcasting resilience, prioritizing risk, and optimizing capital spend across millions of assets. Founded in Australia, Neara operates regionally across ANZ, the USA, and Europe.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Datumate
providers.description: Datumate is a construction technology company whose cloud-native SaaS platform, DatuBIM, turns drone imagery, laser-scanning, and site data into real-time progress tracking, deviation detection, automated reporting, and actionable analytics for heavy civil infrastructure projects. It serves asset owners, general contractors, and engineering and consulting firms across roads, highways, rail, bridges, and earthworks, giving multi-site visibility from design validation through construction to final inspection. The company reports 125+ active customers, thousands of managed sites, and tens of thousands of processed drone flights. Datumate has Israeli engineering roots (Technion) with leadership based in Miami, Florida, and is backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: LocateAI
providers.description: LocateAI (Locate) is an AI-integrated commercial real estate brokerage focused on retail site selection for multi-unit and franchise brands. Its platform pairs proprietary AI models with full-service advisory to help brands choose markets, source and score sites, forecast Year-1 revenue and cannibalization risk, right-size franchise territories, and negotiate leases — from the first market through the signed lease. The models analyze 200M+ mobile devices and 1,100+ variables for device-level trade-area, fair-share, and time-weighted revenue analysis. Locate is delivered as a managed service; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: Piinpoint
providers.description: PiinPoint is an AI-powered location intelligence and site selection platform for retailers, restaurants, brokers, and commercial real estate teams. The software combines demographic, mobile-location, traffic, and competitive data to help teams validate sites, forecast sales, model cannibalization, run network simulations, and plan expansion. Delivered as a B2B SaaS web application (app.piinpoint.com), PiinPoint does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Overstory
providers.description: Overstory provides AI-powered vegetation intelligence for electric utilities and grid operators. The platform fuses high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery with machine learning to detect vegetation encroachment, hazard trees, and wildfire risk along power line corridors, helping utilities prioritize trimming, optimize vegetation management spend, and improve grid reliability (SAIDI). Overstory was founded as 20tree.ai and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. As of this profile the company delivers its intelligence through a customer platform and services rather than a public developer API; no public API documentation, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: EyeLights
providers.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

providers.name: Mozi
providers.description: Mozi is a private social network mobile app founded by Twitter and Medium co-founder Ev Williams and Molly DeWolf Swenson, and backed by Obvious Ventures. Rather than public profiles or follower counts, Mozi privately matches your phone contacts so you learn when friends are in the same city, attending the same events, or checking in nearby — designed to spark in-person "social serendipity" and get people off their screens. Launched in December 2024 and available in 135+ countries, Mozi is a consumer iOS/Android application with no public developer program, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Rever Moto
providers.description: REVER (Rever Moto) is a motorcycle-focused navigation, ride-tracking, and social platform for riders. It offers a web-based route planner and mobile apps (iOS, Android, and Apple CarPlay) that let motorcyclists discover more than 3,000 curated routes worldwide, plan and sync trips, record rides with offline GPS tracking, and get turn-by-turn voice navigation. Social features include live friend tracking, ride sharing, challenges, and stories. REVER offers a free tier and a paid "Pro" subscription, and partners with brands including Honda, Cycle Gear, and Quad Lock. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass REVER publishes no public developer API, documentation, or integration surface — it is a consumer mobile/web product.

providers.name: Orbio
providers.description: Orbio Earth is a climate-tech company (founded 2021; Dover, Delaware, USA and Cologne, Germany) that turns open satellite data into industrial methane intelligence for the energy sector. Its platform detects, quantifies, and tracks methane emissions from oil-and-gas infrastructure globally at asset level with a roughly 5-day revisit rate, using multispectral imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, EMIT) and machine learning, plus Bayesian uncertainty estimation. Customers — oil-and-gas operators and private-equity firms — use it for super-emitter identification, historical trend and root-cause analysis, and compliance with emerging methane regulation. Platform access is offered via the web application or a sales-gated data API integration; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK. Orbio also publishes the open-source Project Eucalyptus methane-detection pipelines on GitHub for research use.

providers.name: Vake
providers.description: VAKE is a Norwegian maritime domain awareness company that detects, identifies, and tracks "dark vessels" from space. The VAKE platform fuses satellite imagery, AIS signals, and machine learning to reveal hidden vessel activity at sea for governments and industry. Its three products are Pathfinder, which reconstructs a vessel's past, present, and predicted movements and searches satellite imagery for vessels that go AIS-dark; Overwatch, which monitors an Area of Interest around ports, critical infrastructure, and economic zones to surface unreported activity such as illegal fishing, transshipments, and spoofing; and Clearview, a machine-learning service that identifies dark-vessel observations in multispectral satellite imagery against a global vessel-signature database spanning 2016 to today. The platform is delivered as a web application (studio.vake.ai) backed by a private API (api.nemme.io); onboarding is sales-led rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Understory
providers.description: Understory is an insurtech company headquartered in Madison, Wisconsin (founded 2012) that combines its own network of ground-truth Dot weather sensors with a proprietary weather risk model to underwrite parametric insurance against severe weather, including hail coverage for automotive dealership open lots and agricultural weather risk. Its UnderstoryOS platform covers broker management, pricing and quoting, and automated weather-triggered claims. Understory publishes no public API or developer portal; the platform is offered to insurance partners rather than as a self-service developer product.

providers.name: VOYGR
providers.description: VOYGR provides real-world place intelligence for AI apps and agents, delivering continuous location and point-of-interest (POI) data validation and enrichment. Its Location Freshness Validation confirms historical existence and current operating status, detecting relocations, rebrands, and closures across multiple attributes with up to 99.62% validation precision and configurable decision thresholds. Its Location Data Enrichment populates and continuously enriches place records from web, social, authoritative, and other sources, spanning foundational attributes (address, contacts, web presence), operating data (hours, menus, prices), and fresh context (articles, reviews, news, events). VOYGR is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) and SNR.VC backed seed-stage company based in San Francisco, founded by Vlad Baskakov (CEO, ex-Google Maps) and Yarik Markov (CTO, ex-Google/Meta/Apple ML). Its maps API goes beyond the 10-15 standard attributes of existing mapping providers. The developer surface is currently demo-gated and no public API documentation is published yet.

providers.name: 2NDNATURE
providers.description: 2NDNATURE is a Santa Cruz, California environmental technology company that builds cloud-based stormwater management and water-quality software. Its flagship product, 2NFORM, is GIS-powered MS4/NPDES compliance software that helps municipalities automate stormwater permit reporting, track assets and BMPs, detect illicit discharges, and run construction and post-construction programs. Rainsteward is its corporate water-stewardship platform for reducing costs and maximizing the value of stormwater investments. The company embeds peer-reviewed environmental science into an enterprise SaaS platform and is backed by Techstars. No public developer API program has been identified; the 2NFORM and Rainsteward applications are gated SaaS logins.

providers.name: Tile (thetileapp)
providers.description: Tile is a consumer Bluetooth-tracker company whose Tile Mate, Pro, Slim, and Sticker devices help people find everyday items such as keys, wallets, bags, and phones, backed by the crowd-sourced Tile "Find" network that anonymously relays location when another Tile user passes a lost item. Founded in 2012, Tile was acquired by Life360 in 2021 and now operates as part of the Life360 family-safety platform. Tile publishes consumer apps for iOS and Android and a support and legal surface, but does not offer an official public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; only third-party community libraries wrap its private app API. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web and security-program surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Duranta
providers.description: Duranta Labs is an applied AI laboratory building geospatial and computer-vision technology to understand the physical world. Its foundation vision model, Aidan, generates accurate, current 4D digital twins from optical imagery. That model powers a Landscapers solution that lets professionals measure, design, and bid any property directly from imagery without a site visit, a general-purpose World Model for spatial intelligence, and a forthcoming AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) product that turns an address into a precise digital model. Duranta is backed by Fifth Wall.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: Bedrock
providers.description: Bedrock (Bedrock Ocean Exploration) builds advanced autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and Mosaic, a cloud-native data platform that transforms how the world maps, monitors, and understands the seafloor. Its AUV fleet carries multibeam echosounder, side-scan sonar, magnetometer, and sub-bottom profiler payloads to deliver high-resolution geophysical survey data for offshore energy (wind, oil and gas, renewables), ports and harbors, submarine telecom infrastructure, defense, and scientific research. A Northzone portfolio company, Bedrock is an enterprise ocean-data provider; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: INGU
providers.description: INGU is a pipeline integrity technology company delivering inline inspection for oil & gas and water/wastewater pipelines through its Pipers multi-sensor free-floating inspection system paired with AI analytics and GIS-based pipeline viewer software. The platform performs leak detection, deposit and wall-condition assessment, and detection of gas pockets, magnetic features, bends, and hot taps across pipelines of any diameter or material. INGU has inspected over 900 pipelines for operators including Chevron, Shell, TotalEnergies, SUEZ, and Vale. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; the company publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Jiobit
providers.description: Jiobit is a real-time GPS tracking device company owned by Life360, based in San Mateo, California. Its lightweight (18g) wearable tracker is designed for kids, pets, seniors, and adults, combining LPWA CatM1 cellular, GPS, WiFi, and BLE for location accuracy of 1-50 feet, up to 30 days of battery life, geofence and SOS/911 emergency alerts, and tamper-proof, government-level encryption. Jiobit is a consumer hardware and mobile-app product sold direct-to-consumer with a monthly connectivity subscription; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: NCX
providers.description: NCX (Natural Capital Exchange), originally founded as SilviaTerra, is a forestry technology company that maps and measures every acre of U.S. forestland using satellite imagery and machine learning. NCX built the Natural Capital Exchange, a marketplace that paid landowners to defer timber harvests and generate forest carbon credits, and it now offers LandBook, a tool that helps landowners capture the story, plans, and practical knowledge behind their property so it can be passed on to the next steward. The company is backed by Union Square Ventures and Version One Ventures.

providers.name: oneNav
providers.description: oneNav is a fabless GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) semiconductor company building the next generation of mobile positioning. Its L5-direct receiver acquires and tracks on the modern L5 satellite band without legacy L1 aiding, delivering higher location accuracy in urban canyons and far greater resilience to GPS jamming and spoofing, in half the RF size, power and cost of hybrid L1+L5 solutions. Founded in 2019 (Steve Poizner, Paul McBurney) with offices in Sunnyvale, CA and Tampere, Finland, oneNav targets smartphones, wearables, IoT trackers, defense and emergency services. It is backed by GV, Norwest Venture Partners and GSR Ventures. oneNav is a hardware/silicon company and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: PierSight Space
providers.description: PierSight Space is an India-based space technology company building a constellation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Automatic Identification System (AIS) satellites for persistent, all-weather maritime surveillance of the world's oceans. Founded by former ISRO engineer Gaurav Seth, PierSight delivers near-real-time ocean monitoring (targeting ~30-minute data latency and 100% ocean coverage) to detect illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, monitor oil spills, protect Exclusive Economic Zones, support maritime insurance risk assessment, and improve shipping operations. The company has raised roughly $8M from investors including Alpha Wave Ventures, Elevation Capital, and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass PierSight sells data solutions to enterprise and government clients and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Renoster Systems
providers.description: Renoster Systems is a carbon-credit ratings agency bringing deep transparency to the nature-based voluntary carbon markets. Using remote sensing, LiDAR, satellite data, and machine learning, Renoster independently rates forestry and other nature-based carbon offset projects, quantifying how much CO2 per credit a project has actually sequestered, and publishes public tools such as its Mercury project database and Renoster/Mercury rubric for researchers, reserve managers, policymakers, and corporate buyers. Renoster is a Techstars-backed startup. As of this profile the company does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; this record captures its company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: World View
providers.description: World View (World View Enterprises) is a Tucson, Arizona-based stratospheric balloon company focused on remote sensing and persistent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). Its uncrewed high-altitude balloons carry EO/FMV, IR, SAR, and hyperspectral sensors for defense, government, and commercial missions. Acquired by Ondas Holdings in 2026, it now operates as part of the Ondas Sentinel multi-domain intelligence platform, with partnerships including Palantir and Sierra Nevada Corporation. World View publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Worldview
providers.description: World View Enterprises (worldview.space) — incorporated in 2012 and headquartered in Tucson, Arizona — operates stratospheric balloons and high-altitude platforms for remote sensing, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), alongside a stratospheric space-tourism program. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company has completed more than 140 stratospheric flight operations for customers including NASA, NOAA, and the U.S. Department of Defense. World View was acquired by Ondas, Inc. in April 2026 and merged with DZYNE Technologies in July 2026 to form Ondas Sentinel. The company publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Zeitview
providers.description: Zeitview (formerly DroneBase) is an AI-powered aerial inspection and asset intelligence platform. It combines a managed network of drone and aircraft pilots with computer-vision analytics and lifecycle asset-management software to deliver inspection imagery, condition assessments, and actionable intelligence for wind energy, solar, utilities, oil & gas, construction, commercial real estate, and property management. As of this profile the company operates a customer web platform, support center, and blog but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; data access is arranged through direct customer engagement.

providers.name: OnXMaps
providers.description: onX Maps (onXmaps) is a Montana-based GPS mapping technology company building offline-capable navigation apps for outdoor recreation. Its product line spans onX Hunt (hunting maps with public/private land boundaries, species and unit data), onX Offroad (650K+ miles of off-road and overland trails), onX Backcountry (hiking, backpacking, skiing and climbing, incorporating Mountain Project and MTB Project data), and onX Fish (lake maps and fishing). The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. onX does not publish a public developer API; this profile is a company record enriched from its public web, security, and trust surfaces rather than an API contract.

providers.name: Sylvera
providers.description: Sylvera is a London-headquartered carbon data and climate intelligence platform — often described as the "Moody's for the voluntary carbon market" — providing independent ratings, market data, and geospatial analytics that help corporate buyers, investors, project developers, governments, and standards bodies make informed decisions across carbon and commodities markets. Founded in 2020 by Allister Furey and Samuel Gill, Sylvera combines remote sensing, machine learning over satellite imagery and LiDAR-derived biomass data, and on-the-ground project assessment to produce letter-graded ratings (e.g., AA, A, B) for carbon credit projects across nature-based (REDD+, ARR, IFM), engineered removals, renewable energy, and cookstove methodologies. The platform's product surface spans Ratings, Market Intelligence (supply, demand, and pricing signals), an Article 6 & CORSIA Hub for compliance risk, a Market Gateway to roughly 400 million tonnes of project inventory, Earth Analytics and a Biomass Atlas for geospatial MRV, and Commodity Insights covering CORSIA, LCFS, CFR, and FuelEU Maritime mechanism eligibility and carbon intensity assessments. Sylvera distributes its data through a web platform, downloadable reports, and a gated Carbon Credit Analytics API (base URL https://api.sylvera.com/v1, JSON API style, API-key auth) used to syndicate ratings and pricing into ESG and sustainability reporting tools such as Workiva, Persefoni, and Watershed. Commercial packaging runs Freemium, Essentials, and Enterprise tiers, with Accelerated Ratings, Market Forecasts, and Geospatial add-ons all sold via contact-sales; there is no public OpenAPI specification, no published SDK, and no Sylvera GitHub organization — the API and full ratings catalog are available only to authenticated enterprise customers.

providers.name: Atmosfy
providers.description: Atmosfy is a live-video mapping platform that bills itself as the world's largest live video map, aggregating 500M+ geo-tagged short-form videos across 100M+ places in 20,000+ cities and 150+ countries. The consumer app lets people see what restaurants, bars, hotels, and events actually look like in real time, while its business side offers brand targeting, embedded local-video integrations for other platforms, and video corpora for AI training. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Atmosfy publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures company identity, legal/link surface, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Geopipe
providers.description: Geopipe uses AI and machine learning to build game-ready digital twins of real-world cities and environments. It ingests raw sensor data (imagery and laser scans) and reconstructs regions as semantically-modeled, multi-level-of- detail 3D models that developers stream or download into games, simulations, training, architecture, and metaverse applications without any manual 3D modeling. Delivery is through Cesium 3D Tiles streaming for Unity and Unreal Engine, downloadable 3D meshes in common file formats, ready-to-use Unity Asset Store packs, and a first-party Unity SDK, backed by an open-source geospatial and 3D-tiles toolchain on GitHub. Founded in New York City by Christopher Mitchell and Thomas Dickerson and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Insitu
providers.description: Insitu Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company that designs, builds, and operates uncrewed aerial systems (UAS) and related intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance technologies for defense and government customers. Its product line includes the Integrator, ScanEagle, and RQ-21A air vehicles alongside imaging payloads, ground control stations, and mission software such as TacitView, the Media Management Suite, and the Tungsten SDK. Insitu delivers end-to-end capabilities for collecting, processing, and distributing information, with more than 1.6 million operational flight hours across 30-plus international customers. Insitu operates as a defense contractor and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Kiki
providers.description: Kiki (Kikihub) is a location-based social networking and chat mobile app that connects people nearby for local friendships, dating, networking, and community conversations. Users join local chat rooms to discover people around them and start real conversations, meeting new friends and matches in their area. The app is available for iOS and Android. Kiki publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile tracks the company within the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed (500 Global, a16z) consumer social lead awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: NNG
providers.description: NNG (NNG Software Developing and Commercial LLC), formerly Nav N Go, is a Budapest-based automotive navigation and location-based software company founded in 2004. Its flagship iGO platform delivers modular guidance, positioning, routing, map content management, and driver-assistance features such as Intelligent Speed Assistance, embedded in more than 60 million devices across 30+ vehicle brands and supplied to over 150 automotive and mobility partners in nearly 200 countries. NNG is backed by growth investment from Insight Partners. NNG sells embedded and OEM location-based software rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or API documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Insurdata
providers.description: Insurdata is a re/insurance technology company providing global, best-in-class geocoding and property exposure data. Its unique multi-sourced methodology delivers the highest-resolution, building-level geocoding available worldwide, together with building-perimeter and property-characteristic data that lets underwriters and catastrophe modelers assess risk at the individual-property level at the point of underwriting. Insurdata's augmented exposure data has been used in collaborative studies with carriers such as Canopius and flood modelers such as Fathom to sharpen exposure levels and average-annual-loss (AAL) forecasts. The company is a portfolio company of Anthemis and serves the global re/insurance market.

providers.name: Skycatch
providers.description: Skycatch built spatial data capture, processing, and analytics for mining and construction sites, turning drone and aerial imagery into high-precision 3D data, volumetrics, and AI-driven site insights. Its products included Spatial Sight, Spatial DataHub (datahub.skycatch.com), and EdgeServer for on-site edge processing. Skycatch was acquired by Caterpillar Inc. on July 7, 2026 (following Caterpillar's RPMGlobal acquisition) to expand its mining technology capabilities. A developer platform exists at docs.skycatch.com but is password-gated, and no public API specification is available. Originally surfaced as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company.

providers.name: Earth AI
providers.description: Earth AI is a vertically integrated, AI-powered mineral exploration company that discovers, develops, and owns critical mineral mines for the emerging hardware economy — data centers, humanoid robots, eVTOL aircraft, fusion energy, space, and defense. Its proprietary predictive model, MTP, is trained on roughly 400 million geological sites to identify the source rocks of new mineral deposits and dramatically compress traditional exploration timelines. The company vertically integrates the search for critical minerals: it predicts targets with AI, acquires mineral rights, and drills to prove and own the resource. Earth AI is backed by DCVC and has been profiled by TechCrunch, Business Insider, and The Generalist's Future 50. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Earth AI does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Pano
providers.description: Pano AI provides enterprise-grade, AI-powered wildfire and bushfire detection. The platform combines ultra-high-definition 360-degree mountaintop cameras, satellite feeds, field sensor data, and machine learning to detect ignitions early, confirm and triangulate their location, and deliver real-time visual situational intelligence to utilities, fire agencies, first responders, and landowners. Operators access the Pano 360 platform at 360.pano.ai to monitor camera networks, review AI detections, and coordinate incident response. Backed by DCVC and Initialized Capital, Pano was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Rexby
providers.description: Rexby is a consumer travel discovery and trip-planning platform where local creators publish interactive travel guides and maps of curated "spots," and travelers browse those guides, build personal itineraries, and follow creator recommendations. The product is delivered as iOS and Android mobile apps plus the rexby.com web experience, with a creator program that lets travel enthusiasts monetize their guides. Backed by Techstars. As of this profile Rexby publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this apis.yml captures its identity and a domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SATIM
providers.description: SATIM provides AI-powered analysis of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) operations. Its OREC analytics engine performs automated object detection and classification on satellite and airborne SAR data (accuracy up to 95%), deployable in cloud, edge, or air-gapped environments and integrable into C2 and C4ISR workflows. OREC-Intelligence adds persistent monitoring with real-time area-of-interest change alerts and activity pattern analysis. Headquartered in Krakow, Poland, with offices in Dover, Delaware and London. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation are published at this time.

providers.name: TrustPoint
providers.description: TrustPoint, Inc. is a space technology company building a fully commercial, next-generation global navigation satellite system (GNSS) — a C-band LEO microsatellite constellation delivering secure positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) independent of GPS, with improved accuracy, faster time to first fix, and anti-jamming / anti-spoofing capabilities for automotive, aviation, critical infrastructure, and national security applications. Headquartered in Northern Virginia with an office in Mountain View, California, and backed by DCVC, TrustPoint does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Esper Satellite Imagery
providers.description: Esper Satellite Imagery is an Australian space-technology company building an 18-satellite hyperspectral Earth-observation constellation (the Over The Rainbow / OTR program) to deliver global chemical-composition data of the planet's surface from orbit. Its Esperesso hyperspectral imagers capture more than 100 contiguous spectral bands spanning roughly 400 to 1000 nm, which Esper turns into mineralisation maps that identify lithium, rare earths, gold, nickel, cobalt and alteration zones for critical-mineral exploration — faster, cheaper and greener than traditional ground surveys. Founded in 2021 in Melbourne, Victoria by Iqbal and Joey Lorenczak, Esper sells custom area-of-interest mineral maps and a pre-built Northern Territory mineral map. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, security and code-repository surface.

providers.name: Aerodyne
providers.description: Aerodyne Group is a Malaysia-headquartered DT3 (drone technology, data technology, and digital transformation) enterprise solutions provider, founded in 2014. Through its Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) model and the AI-powered, cloud-based vertikaliti asset-management platform, Aerodyne turns aerial and sensor data into deep analytics and actionable insights for infrastructure, power line, wind turbine, solar, and agricultural (Agrimor) asset inspection and management. Operating across 45 countries with a global network of AeroRangers, it was ranked the world's number-one drone service provider by Drone Industry Insights in 2021 and 2022. Aerodyne is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable specification has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Brumby
providers.description: Brumby (formerly GrazeMate) is a Y Combinator-backed (W2026) precision-grazing company based in Sydney, Australia, building an autonomous drone toolkit for cattle ranchers. Brumby drones plan routes and move herds with gentle, AI-guided pressure, fly scheduled monitoring missions that locate and count every animal, measure standing dry-matter pasture biomass from the air, and inspect water troughs, tanks and fences on every flight — all managed from a single phone app that works online or in a local base-station mode without connectivity. The company is running pilot programs and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is a company lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Involve Space
providers.description: Involve Space is an Italian stratospheric aerospace company building real-time Earth intelligence. It operates autonomous high-altitude balloon platforms (Stratostats) that loiter around 20 kilometers for hours, days, or weeks to deliver continuous, high-resolution Earth observation, bridging the gap between satellites, drones, and ground sensors. Its Neurostar AI flight software autonomously controls individual balloons and networks of them (LoonHive), while the CLEAR GeoAI platform turns captured imagery into geospatial insights for disaster response, infrastructure and environmental monitoring, security, and in-orbit-demonstration / payload validation. A certified B Corporation headquartered in Italy with U.S. operations at the Houston Spaceport, Involve Space is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, CDP Venture Capital, and an EIC Accelerator grant.

providers.name: Vermeer
providers.description: Vermeer is an American-Ukrainian defense-technology startup (founded 2018 by Brian Streem; headquartered in New York with forward operations in Kyiv) building vision-based autonomy for unmanned aerial platforms. Its Visual Positioning System (VPS) uses electro-optical and infrared cameras plus onboard AI (NVIDIA) to match imagery to 2D/3D maps and deliver precise navigation in GPS-denied, jammed, or spoofed environments. Products include Air (absolute positioning without GPS), Celestial (star-based navigation), and Terminal Guidance (precision targeting). The technology has been fielded by the Armed Forces of Ukraine and is aimed at defense customers including Lockheed Martin, General Atomics, Northrop Grumman, and the U.S. Air Force and Army. Vermeer exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time; this profile is a company/marketing surface with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Windward
providers.description: Windward is a Maritime AI company headquartered in London and Washington D.C. delivering mission-grade, multi-source maritime intelligence for defense agencies, law enforcement, customs, energy and commodity traders, marine insurers, shippers, and financial institutions. Founded by CEO Ami Daniel, Windward fuses AIS data, remote sensing (EO, SAR, RF GEOINT), proprietary behavioral analytics, and generative AI into a single Maritime AI platform covering vessel screening, ownership and entity resolution, sanctions exposure, deceptive shipping detection, ship-to-ship transfer analysis, IUU fishing detection, smuggling detection, container tracking, and maritime infrastructure protection. Windward exposes its intelligence through the API Insights Lab, a unified GraphQL API at developer.windward.ai providing programmatic access to vessel risk scores, Organization Defined Risk (ODR), ultimate beneficial ownership, early detection signals, tracked shipments, carriers, and detention & demurrage data, along with webhooks and workflow automation. The company has no public REST/OpenAPI surface, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub org — its API is GraphQL-only with managed onboarding and expert-led implementation support.

providers.name: Climavision
providers.description: Climavision is a Louisville, Kentucky weather intelligence company that combines a proprietary nationwide supplemental network of low-altitude X-band, dual-polarization gap-filling weather radars with AI-driven numerical weather prediction (NWP) to deliver enterprise-grade forecasts and observational data. Its Horizon AI product line includes Horizon Point for site-specific forecasts, Horizon Global for ground-to-high- altitude global models, Horizon HI-RES for custom high-resolution local forecasting, and Horizon S2S for subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction. Climavision exposes a Weather API hosted at point-forecast-api.climavision.com with 1,800+ parameters, 15-day forecasts, and bearer-token authentication, plus a separate Radar Status API and Radar-as-a-Service offering that supplies Level II files, NetCDF, and GeoTIFF radar data products (reflectivity, velocity, dual-pol-derived QPE at 1km, precipitation type, tornado debris detection) for coverage below 4,000 feet where NEXRAD cannot see due to Earth curvature. The company integrates its radar feed into MRMS and has provided supplemental data into the National Weather Service's AWIPS software.
